predictor.notes: Best observation-consistent hypothesis: a minimum charge of 92092 cents, followed by 21693 + 415*q, then a 14% discount on that linear formula. After rounding, this predictor reproduces all 10 observed prices exactly: eight distinct estimates and the two approvals. Interval fitting confirms feasibility. Important uncertainty: the minimum-charge transition at 170 is inferred from the intersection of the constant and linear formulas, not directly observed. Under the three-segment hypothesis, the discount starts somewhere in the inclusive range 301..327; 314 is a midpoint estimate, not an identified threshold. Predictions within 301..326 are consequently especially uncertain: the two pricing formulas differ there by approximately 20525–21978 cents. Integer observations also leave some coefficient and one-cent rounding ambiguity. The estimate cap is exhausted; unrestricted nonlinear or additional piecewise behavior between observations cannot be excluded, so exact reconstruction at every quantity is not established.
